612R procedure (operator): Board the cab. 1. Lower the ladder with the ground-level ladder switch. 2. Climb the ladder and open the cab door. 3. Sit down, close the door, and raise the ladder from the CommandARM.

612R procedure (operator): Unfold the boom for field operation. 1. Stop the machine on level ground with overhead clearance. Put it in Park. 2. Raise the boom to full height so the wings clear the cradles and tires. 3. Swing both main wings out (fold OUT). 4. Unfold both outer wings. 5. Lower the boom to spray height (typically 50-76 cm above the target).

612R procedure (operator): Fold the boom for transport. 1. Turn master spray OFF and stop the machine. 2. Level both wings (tilt to 0) and raise the boom to full height. 3. Fold both outer wings IN onto the inner wings. 4. Fold both main wings IN until they rest in the cradles. 5. Lower the boom until the wings rest in the cradles, then select Road mode.

612R procedure (operator): Adjust tread width (120-160 in). 1. Find a firm, level area with room to drive slowly in a straight line. 2. Take the machine out of Park and drive slowly forward. 3. Hold the tread WIDER (or NARROWER) switch until the display shows the target width. 4. Stop, and confirm the tread width on all four legs.

612R procedure (operator): Drive forward with the hydro handle. 1. Start the engine, raise the ladder, take the machine out of Park. 2. Push the hydro handle forward to accelerate. Pull it back to slow down.

612R procedure (mechanic): Open the engine compartment for daily service. 1. Park the machine, lower the boom, stop the engine, remove the key. 2. Release the hood latch and raise the engine hood. 3. Check engine oil at the dipstick. 4. Inspect the air filter restriction indicator and housing. 5. Drain water from the fuel filter / water separator. 6. Inspect the cooling package for debris.

612R procedure (operator): Clean the solution system strainers. 1. Turn master spray off and park. Relieve system pressure. 2. Suction strainer (20 mesh): close the tank valve and remove the bowl. 3. Pressure strainer (50 mesh). 4. Boom strainer (80 mesh), at the centre frame.

612R procedure (operator): Fill using the side fill and chemical eductor. 1. Park the machine and lower the ladder for access. 2. Connect the water supply to the 3 in quick-fill coupler. 3. Lower the chemical eductor to working height. 4. When you finish, rinse the eductor and raise it to the stowed position.
612R moving part: Front steer angle (outer wheel). Range -28 to 28 deg. asin(wheelbase / turning radius) = 27.9 deg. The inner wheel follows Ackermann geometry.
612R moving part: Tread width. Range 3.05 to 4.06 m. Rate is an ESTIMATE. Hydraulic tread adjust only moves while the machine is rolling (see interlocks).
612R moving part: Air-ride strut travel. Range -0.1 to 0.1 m.
612R moving part: Boom nozzle height. Range 0.5 to 2.45 m. Parallel-link lift: height = pivot_z + L*sin(theta) - nozzle_drop. The centre frame counter-rotates to stay level.
612R moving part: Left wing tilt. Range -8 to 18 deg.
612R moving part: Right wing tilt. Range -8 to 18 deg.
612R moving part: Left main fold. Range 0 to 90 deg.
612R moving part: Right main fold. Range 0 to 90 deg.
612R moving part: Left outer fold. Range 0 to 178 deg.
612R moving part: Right outer fold. Range 0 to 178 deg.
612R moving part: Left breakaway. Range -35 to 35 deg. Spring breakaway swings both ways when it hits something, then springs back to 0.
612R moving part: Right breakaway. Range -35 to 35 deg.
612R moving part: Hydraulic ladder. Range 0 to 80 deg. Hydraulic raise/lower is OFFICIAL; travel angle is an ESTIMATE.
612R moving part: Cab door. Range 0 to 80 deg.
612R moving part: Engine hood (front nose, tilts up). Range 0 to 65 deg.
612R moving part: Chemical eductor. Range 0 to 85 deg.
612R moving part: Hydro handle (MFWD lever). Range -12 to 25 deg. Forward = forward travel. Lever angle maps to the commanded fraction of the selected range.
612R moving part: Steering wheel. Range -540 to 540 deg. About 3 turns lock to lock (ESTIMATE). It drives the steer joint.
